newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Unibanco strong in debut.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Unibanco strong in debut.

text.p: Brazilian bank Unibanco Group SA was off to a strong start in active trading on the New York Stock Exchange Thursday, highlighting trade in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Traders in Latin American ADRs said activity was weighed by concern over the falling 30-year U.S. Treasury bond.
The long bond was off 13/32 to yield seven percent. A higher yield tends to attract money away from Latin American shares.
"Everybody is basically holding their breath and watching the long bond," a trader said.

Unibanco, the third-biggest private bank in Brazil, was trading at 34-1/8 in early afternoon after being priced at 33-3/4. Volume was 6.45 million ADRs, putting Unibanco at the top of the New York Stock Exchange's most-active list.
The ADRs represent 500 units of two shares each. Unibanco was offering 33 percent of the bank's preferred shares and two-thirds of the holding company's preferred shares.
Both shares in the unit are non-voting.
Nuno Fernandes, a Latin American banks analyst at ING Barings, said increased liquidity made the ADRs attractive.
Fernades has rated Unibanco a buy.
Among other Latin American shares, Brazilian telecom easing from an intraday record of 129-1/8.
The ADR was helped by a congressional committee's approval of a bill regulating the privatization of the telecommunications sector, a trader said.
Among European ADRs, Swedish telephone equipment company Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson rose 9/16 to 36-3/4 after reaching a 12-month intraday high of 37.

Canada's Cineplex Odeon rose 1/4 to 2-1/8 after it reported a first quarter profit of $0.01 a share compared with a loss of $0.06 a share in the same period a year ago. Its volume of 1.4 million shares put it among the most-actively traded foreign companies.
Decliners led advancers 256 to 209 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group fell 0.14 percent and volume was 40.5 million ADRs.
